months.title: Responsible AI use
weeks: Record how you currently use AI. Explain one recent assignment without AI. Begin the course introduction.
Write your own attempt before opening AI. Ask for hints and explanations. Study the course’s basic prompting lessons.
Check three AI claims against original sources. Open every reference used. Keep private information out of prompts.
Complete two short study sessions without AI each week. Close the tool and explain what you learned. Review with your sibling.
months.result: One-page AI agreement, five use examples, and one corrected AI claim.

resource.title: Prompt Engineering for Everyone — IBM Cognitive Class

months.title: Better questions and AI feedback
weeks: Continue the same course. Practise context + your attempt + exact difficulty + requested help.
Improve five vague questions from your actual coursework. Ask AI to quiz you one question at a time.
Draft your own answer. Ask AI to identify missing evidence or unclear reasoning without rewriting it.
Finish relevant course lessons. Explain three concepts without the tool. Use brief, checkable explanations and verify answers.
months.result: Ten improved questions and three before-and-after examples of your own reasoning.

resource.title: Prompt Engineering for Everyone — IBM Cognitive Class

months.title: Independent thinking and evidence in the age of AI
weeks: Watch the TED video. Separate a claim, supporting evidence and an opinion in one article. Identify where AI could replace your own thinking.
Trace one online claim to its original source. Check author, date, context and what the source actually supports.
Compare two explanations of the same issue. Write the strongest evidence for each and what remains unknown.
Investigate one AI answer independently. Write your conclusion first, then invite criticism of it.
months.result: Four source checks, including one AI claim. Explain your conclusion and uncertainty without AI.

resource.title: How to stop AI from killing your critical thinking — Advait Sarkar, TED

months.title: Social media for career: LinkedIn + Instagram or TikTok; then career in the age of AI
weeks: Weeks 1–2: Study the free Social Media Marketing course. Build an accurate LinkedIn student profile and choose Instagram or TikTok to showcase your original journalism work.
Weeks 1–2: Follow credible journalists and newsrooms. Publish one original learning reflection on LinkedIn and one useful post on your chosen second platform. Check facts, permissions and privacy.

Week 3: Career in the age of AI. Compare reporting, editing and communications roles. List tasks AI can assist with and skills you must practise yourself: verification, interviewing, judgement and original writing.
Week 4: Choose two career directions to explore. Identify one campus activity for each. Explain your choices without AI and review them with your sibling.
months.result: Accurate LinkedIn profile, one second platform, two original posts and a one-page career map showing AI-assisted tasks and human responsibilities.

resource.title: Social Media Marketing — HubSpot Academy (free course)

months.title: Digital organisation and security
weeks: Study Internet Safety. Create unit folders, a source notebook and a clearly labelled portfolio folder.
Use unique passwords and two-step verification. Check recovery details and document-sharing permissions.
Back up important coursework. Build a calendar of deadlines and practise recognising suspicious links and messages.
Demonstrate safe sharing and restoring a backed-up file. Record where coursework, sources and final work belong.
months.result: Organised files, deadline calendar, secure accounts and a tested backup. Never show passwords at review.

months.title: Self-management and learning habits
weeks: Study Learning how to learn. Plan one realistic week around lectures, rest, meals, worship and study.
After lectures, close notes and recall key ideas. Keep phone notifications off during focused study.
Track spending and missed deadlines. Adjust one habit causing difficulty. Ask a lecturer for help when needed.
Review four weeks of your routine. Keep what worked and remove unnecessary activities. Plan exam weeks lightly.
months.result: Four weekly plans, a simple spending record and evidence of learning without reminders.

months.title: Discovering strengths through coursework
weeks: Study only Weeks 1–2 of Succeed in the workplace. Identify interests, values and activities you voluntarily return to.
Gather three coursework examples and lecturer feedback. Record your contribution to group work.
Use one campus or church activity to try a small responsibility. Request specific feedback on what you did well.
Compare enjoyment, quality, improvement and initiative across examples. Choose two promising strengths for further practice.
months.result: A strengths record supported by three pieces of work and feedback. No fixed personality label.

months.title: Professional communication and relationships
weeks: Study Business Communication. Write a clear email with a useful subject line, context and one specific request.
Practise a 30-second introduction. Ask a lecturer or senior student one purposeful question.
Have two further conversations about study, career paths or practical opportunities. Record what you learned.
Follow up politely and apply one piece of feedback. Discuss how you responded to criticism or disagreement.
months.result: Professional introduction, three purposeful conversations and a feedback-and-follow-up record.

months.title: Digital audiences and content planning
weeks: Study Social Media Marketing. Define one audience, its needs and the purpose of a small content project.
Make a four-week content calendar for a campus club or personal project. Obtain permission before managing an account.
Publish two useful items based on your own work. Label promotional work and keep reporting independent.
Compare engagement and audience feedback. Explain one change you would make. Confirm your main strength and supporting skill.
months.result: Content calendar, two published items and an evidence-based improvement. Use the strength record from Month 7.

months.title: Portfolio and clear personal positioning
weeks: Study Resume Writing. Select six existing pieces that show your strongest skills and permission to share.
Write a one-page student CV. Use accurate education, activities, skills and evidence of your own contributions.
Organise a view-only portfolio folder with a contents document. For each piece, state your role, date and what it demonstrates.
Ask a lecturer or editor for feedback. Revise the CV and portfolio. Test the shared link in a signed-out window.
months.result: One-page CV, six-piece portfolio and a clear two-sentence professional introduction.

months.title: Finding and evaluating opportunities
weeks: Return to selected sections of Succeed in the workplace: opportunities, networks, applications and action planning.
Identify six suitable student opportunities through campus media, local publications or communications teams. Verify the organisation.
Prepare and send two tailored applications or pitches. Clarify duties, hours, payment and ownership before accepting work.
Send two more tailored applications or pitches. Record follow-up dates. Never pay an application or recruitment fee.
months.result: Four genuine applications or pitches, a follow-up tracker and one realistic next action.

months.title: Independent work and next-year planning
weeks: Study Freelancing 101. Choose one small project in your strongest area. Agree scope, audience, deadline and permissions.
Write a simple task plan and deliver the first draft. Use AI only after your own attempt and record how it helped.
Request feedback, revise and deliver. Keep scope manageable. Paid work is optional, not a completion requirement.
Evaluate the project yourself. Update your portfolio and write a 90-day plan. Lead the final sibling review.
months.result: One completed project, updated portfolio and a self-written 90-day plan with clear goals.

habits.title: Monthly learning
habits.how: Use only the month’s assigned resource. Months 1–2 share one course. Month 4 covers social media first, then career in the age of AI. Month 7 uses only Weeks 1–2 of the career course.
habits.evidence: Explain one useful idea in your own words.

habits.title: Practical application
habits.how: Complete the weekly task using actual coursework or a small campus activity. Two short sessions should be without AI.
habits.evidence: Keep your original attempt and revised result.

habits.title: Independent reading
habits.how: Read one substantial news item. Identify its claim, evidence and unanswered questions.
habits.evidence: Three brief notes written without AI.

habits.title: Weekly reflection
habits.how: Record what worked, what was difficult and one next action.
habits.evidence: A dated entry in your notebook.

habits.title: Faith reading
habits.how: Read Mind, Character, and Personality, Volume 1 for 15 minutes twice weekly. Read in order at your own pace.
habits.evidence: One idea, one question and one action.

rules.title: Attempt first
rules.text: Spend at least 15 minutes reading, thinking or drafting before using AI. Save your initial attempt.

rules.title: Ask for limited help
rules.text: Ask for hints, examples, a quiz or criticism. Ask the tool not to replace your answer.

rules.title: Verify
rules.text: Check factual claims against original sources. Open references. Never invent quotes, sources, interviewees or observations.

rules.title: Explain independently
rules.text: Close AI and notes. Explain the concept yourself. If you cannot, return to the material.

rules.title: Respect rules and privacy
rules.text: Follow each lecturer’s AI rules. Do not upload private source material, classmates’ details or confidential work.

rules.title: Question template
rules.text: I am working on __. My understanding is __. I tried __. I am stuck on __. Help me by __.

rules.title: Example prompt
rules.text: I wrote this interpretation myself. Ask three questions that reveal gaps in my reasoning. Do not rewrite my answer.

rules.title: Social media routine
rules.text: Use LinkedIn for professional visibility and Instagram or TikTok to showcase original journalism work. Keep notifications off during study. Limit recreational scrolling to 30 minutes daily.

rules.title: Strengths record
rules.text: From Month 1, save coursework and feedback. Record enjoyment, quality, improvement and initiative. Identify two promising strengths at Month 7, then a main and supporting skill at Month 9.

rules.title: Faith reflection
rules.text: Read devotionally. Discuss questions honestly. Use the book for faith and character reflection rather than as a scientific psychology textbook.

rules.title: Free learning
rules.text: All assigned learning resources are free. A free account may be needed. Use the specified lessons rather than adding more courses. Learning links checked 2 October 2026.

rules.title: Annual outcome
rules.text: Six strong portfolio pieces, one independent project, four applications or pitches, and a self-written 90-day plan.
